name: Prize crossword No 24,767
preamble: Seven solutions are closely related; their clues lack further definition

clue.text: First composition in biro?

indicators.note: one thing set inside another is held within its outer letters

blocks.note: Bic is a familiar brand of ballpoint, as Biro is
a composer's first work is Op. 1, written OP I

explanation.surface: A first essay or school composition written out with a ballpoint pen.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the seven film genres the preamble links, so there is no definition. Op. is short for opus, the numbering of a composer's works.
explanation.definitionFit: A biopic is a biographical film, a movie category telling a real person's life story, so it joins the other cinema types.

clue.text: Evens out bulk user

indicators.note: the even-numbered positions are thrown away, keeping only the odd ones

blocks.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Someone buying in bulk spreads the cost evenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evens out' reads as a verb meaning levels, but tells you to remove letters two, four, six and eight.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue movie is a pornographic film, so this colour word names one more category of cinema.

clue.text: Thrust ISP into nothing 1 down

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it

blocks.note: nought, the letter O
BT is a large British internet service provider
the answer at 1 down is BLUE, which also means smutty

explanation.surface: An internet provider forced into a lowly position.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference supplies a synonym of another answer: blue jokes are rude ones. BT, British Telecom, is the UK's main phone and broadband company.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtrude is to push something forward or force it upon others, so as verbs the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Expand lest soldiers invade

indicators.note: invaders get inside the territory they attack

blocks.note: 'lest' means 'in case'
Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Grow larger in case troops come over the border.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is the usual crossword abbreviation for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to grow or make larger in size or amount, a straightforward synonym pair.

clue.text: Rascal dumping LA opera house on jester

indicators.note: to dump something is to discard it, so letters are dropped

blocks.note: La Scala in Milan, with its LA removed
a wag is a joker

explanation.surface: A rogue tips a Los Angeles opera house onto a clown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'LA' looks like Los Angeles, but it is the first word of La Scala, the famous Milan opera house, and is the part removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalawag (or scallywag) is a mischievous rogue, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Fake aristocrat hugs tree, if rumbled

indicators.note: a hug wraps arms round someone, so one piece encloses another
rumbled suggests tumbled and disturbed, so the letters are thrown about

blocks.note: a count is a nobleman
these six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A phoney nobleman pretends to be a tree-hugger, in case he is found out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rumbled' in the surface means found out, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Counterfeit means forged or imitation, the same sense as fake used as an adjective.

clue.text: Cat pinching a king's piece of breathing apparatus

indicators.note: to pinch is to grip something between fingers, so it is held inside

blocks.note: a lynx is a wild cat
taken as written
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A cat steals part of a king's breathing gear.
explanation.walkthrough: R, from Latin rex, is the standard abbreviation for king.
explanation.definitionFit: The larynx, or voice box, sits at the top of the windpipe and forms part of the respiratory tract.

clue.text: The Guardian's back!

blocks.note: a newspaper speaking of itself uses the editorial 'we', and this puzzle appears in the Guardian
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A triumphant announcement that the newspaper has returned.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is writing in the Guardian, so the paper refers to itself as 'we'.
explanation.definitionFit: A western is a film set on the American frontier with cowboys, one of the classic movie genres.

clue.text: Ancient beast, not initially hideous, to see other side of river  …

indicators.note: 'not initially' means without its opening letter

blocks.note: ugly losing its first letter
PTO, please turn over, tells a reader to see the other side of the page
the Don is a river in Russia and in England

explanation.surface: A prehistoric creature, not quite ugly, wants to see the far bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis leads into 12 down, whose definition 'another' means another ancient beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The glyptodon was a huge armoured prehistoric relative of the armadillo, extinct since the Ice Age.

clue.text: Needing fresh air, cut nettle

indicators.note: something made fresh is renewed, so the letters are formed anew

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener cutting nettles needs a breath of fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh air' reads as one phrase, but 'fresh' acts on the letters of both 'air' and 'cut'.
explanation.definitionFit: Urtica is the botanical genus name of the stinging nettle plants.

clue.text: Rope lassoing bird circling South Island

indicators.note: a lasso loops round its catch and holds it
circling something means going all the way round it

blocks.note: a guy is a rope holding a tent or mast steady
the erne is the sea eagle
the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A cowboy ropes a bird flying round New Zealand's South Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South Island' looks like the New Zealand place name, but South is just S and Island alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Guernsey is one of the Channel Islands, lying off the French coast but a British Crown dependency.

clue.text: Officer's paper about fairy facing death when camping?

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer piece goes round the inner

blocks.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
a peri is a fairy in Persian myth
campers sleep under canvas, so what is camping sits inside this shelter
death is one's end

explanation.surface: A police officer's newspaper runs a story about a fairy who dies on a camping trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The tent never appears in the clue: 'when camping' puts the death inside one. Peri is a crossword favourite for fairy, and the Sun is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: A superintendent is a senior police officer rank in Britain, above inspector.

clue.text: …  hot, hairy scout dismembered another

definitions.note: stands for 'another ancient beast', carried over from 8 down

indicators.note: something dismembered is torn limb from limb, so its parts are scattered

blocks.note: H for hot, as on a tap
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prehistoric beast tears apart a sweaty, hairy scout.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 8 down, so 'another' means another ancient beast. 'Hot' gives only its abbreviation H, not all three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The ichthyosaur was a dolphin-shaped marine reptile of the dinosaur era, so it is a second extinct creature.

clue.text: Third composition secures about three shillings for posh garment

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters are arranged anew
to secure is to hold fast, so one piece is held inside

blocks.note: the five letters rearranged
re means concerning
S is the abbreviation for shilling, an old British coin worth one twentieth of a pound

explanation.surface: A third piece of music pays for some fancy clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue echoes 1 across's 'First composition', but here 'composition' signals rearranging the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress shirt is a formal shirt worn with evening dress or a dinner jacket, hence a smart item of clothing.

clue.text: Control panel shows theologian cuddling pig under tree

indicators.note: cuddling wraps around, so one piece encloses the rest
in a down clue, being under means coming after

blocks.note: the ash is a tree
a boar is a male pig
Doctor of Divinity

explanation.surface: A cartoon on a control panel: a scholar hugging a pig beneath a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is the usual crossword abbreviation for a theologian.
explanation.definitionFit: The dashboard of a car holds its instruments and switches, the panel from which a driver controls it.

clue.text: Woman to overeat

indicators.note: turning something over flips it end to end

blocks.note: eat means dine; the 'over' at its front is the turnaround signal

explanation.surface: A woman who tends to eat too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overeat' is one word in the surface but splits into 'over' and 'eat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a female first name, and crosswords freely use any woman's name for 'woman'.

clue.text: Star player turned out in new visor

indicators.note: something turned faces the other way
new means made afresh, so the letters take a fresh order
placed in means set inside

blocks.note: taken as written
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A star sportsman turns out wearing a new visor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned out' reads as 'appeared', but 'turned' acts on 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso is a performer of outstanding skill, especially a musician, so a star performer.

clue.text: Second's not infrequently subdued

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
not infrequently means often, oft

explanation.surface: A second-in-command is often rather quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'has' or 'with', putting S ahead of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft and subdued both describe muted sound, light or colour, gentle rather than harsh.

clue.text: Exploit flower

blocks.note: a feat is a notable deed
a flower is something that flows: the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword trick for river, something that flows, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A feature is a full-length film, the main item on a cinema programme, so it belongs with the other film types.

clue.text: Ancient Syrian kitchen implement holding garden implement back in 10 etc

indicators.note: going back means running the other way
what holds something keeps it inside

blocks.note: a pan is a cooking vessel
a hoe is a weeding tool
turned round
10 across, Guernsey, and the others make up the Channel Islands, CI

explanation.surface: An ancient Syrian frying pan with a garden hoe tucked in it, back on Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' applies only to 'in', and '10 etc' points to Guernsey and its fellow Channel Islands, abbreviated CI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Phoenicians lived on the coast of ancient Syria, in what is now Lebanon, so Phoenician serves as an ancient Syrian.

clue.text: Recipe ironed out, as all should be

indicators.note: out suggests disorder, so the letters are taken apart and remade

blocks.note: R stands for recipe, the Latin 'take' on prescriptions
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe set out tidily, the way everything ought to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ironed out' sounds like a finished, smoothed result, but 'out' signals rearranging. R for recipe comes from prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: Things in order are neat and properly arranged, which is how everything ideally ought to be.

clue.text: Winding up the French with tears

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: French feminine 'the'
a tear is a rip

explanation.surface: A French lover's affair ends in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winding up' reads as a single phrase meaning ending, but splits into the definition and the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiral staircase is a winding one: as an adjective, spiral means coiling or twisting round.

clue.text: Ibo joining anti-poll tax riot?

indicators.note: a riot is disorder, so the letters run wild

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Nigerian joins the 1990 poll tax riots in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ibo (Igbo) are a Nigerian people; the poll tax was a British local tax whose 1990 protests ended in rioting in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Blaxploitation was a 1970s American film genre made with black casts for black audiences, like Shaft.

clue.text: Held up by marionette

indicators.note: what is held by something is contained within it
in a down clue, up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: letters three to six

explanation.surface: A puppet on strings holds itself up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held up' sounds like delayed or supported, but splits into two separate signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Film noir is the shadowy 1940s crime-thriller style of cinema, often just called noir.

clue.text: Collector dropping bits of tin for member of house?

indicators.note: dropping things means letting them fall away

blocks.note: an antiquarian collects antiques or old books
each of the three letters taken out separately

explanation.surface: A collector melting down scraps of tin for a member of the Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' suggests Parliament, but it is an astrological house, the sign of Aquarius; the letters T, I and N are removed separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born under Aquarius is an Aquarian, one of those belonging to that zodiac sign or house.

clue.text: Magic circles following others into disease

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it
coming after means placed later in the line

blocks.note: venereal disease
other circles, a second pair of letter Os
two rings, two letter Os

explanation.surface: Magic circles, the conjurors' clubs, spread like a disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magic circles' looks like the conjurors' society, but splits into the definition and the letters. 'Others' means other circles, so there are two pairs of rings.
explanation.definitionFit: Voodoo is a religion of Haiti associated with sorcery, so the word means magic or witchcraft.

clue.text: D-Dickensian family's residents?

blocks.note: the stammered letter taken as written
Sam Weller and his father Tony in The Pickwick Papers

explanation.walkthrough: The stutter supplies a lone D. Sam Weller is Mr Pickwick's cockney servant in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwellers are people who live in a place, the same as its inhabitants or occupants.

clue.text: God's not beginning to take gold

indicators.note: without a start means the opening letter goes

blocks.note: Thor, the Norse thunder god, losing his first letter
R is short for recipe, Latin for 'take'
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A deity declines to accept gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Recipe, abbreviated R, is Latin for 'take', heading old prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: Horror is the film genre built to frighten, with monsters, ghosts and slashers, one of the cinema types.
